original_title: Injectable Hydrogels for Programmable Protein Release.
title: Hydrogels timed to release protein on a schedule
blurb: Injectable hydrogels built to dole out protein payloads on a program rather than dumping it all at once. No release curves or specific protein targets given.

original_title: Enantioselective Construction, by Nickel(II)-Catalyzed Desymmetrization, of Tetrahydropentalen-1(2 H )-ones Incorporating Angular Fluorine and Hydroxy Groups
title: Fluorine and a hydroxyl land on the same ring corner via nickel desymmetrization
blurb: A Ni(II)-catalyzed desymmetrizing arylative cyclization of fluorinated propargyl cyclopentanediones builds tetrahydropentalenones carrying angular fluorine and hydroxy groups, up to 87% yield and 96:4 er. Some of the products also slow MCF-7 breast cancer cells, though that's a side screen, not the point of the paper.

original_title: Elizabeth Smyth, MD, on Gastric/GEJ Cancer: Novel CLDN18.2-Targeting ADC - The ASCO Post
title: An oncologist's take on the new CLDN18.2 ADC in gastric cancer
blurb: Elizabeth Smyth walks through where the CLDN18.2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate fits for gastric and GEJ cancer. It's a clinician's rundown rather than a trial readout, so don't expect numbers here.

original_title: Dianionic α-Iminopyridinyl Rare-Earth Metal Complexes for Catalytic Hydroborative Amide Reduction
title: Rare-earth catalysts that reduce amides with a borane instead of hydride reagents
blurb: A diamine-pyridine ligand wrapped around five different rare-earth metals, Y, Sm, Dy, Er, and Yb, gives dianionic amido or alkyl complexes that catalyze hydroborative amide reduction. Mostly a ligand-design and structure paper: five flavors of the same scaffold put through one reaction.

original_title: Ligand-Controlled Regiodivergent Boracarboxylation of 1,2-Dienes Using Carbon Dioxide and Copper Catalysts
title: One ligand swap flips which carboxylate you get from CO2 and an allene
blurb: A Cu-catalyzed boracarboxylation of 1,2-dienes where PCy3 steers the product to the alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylate and PtBu3 flips it to the beta,gamma isomer, with CO2 as the carbon source throughout. Same substrate, same metal, opposite regiochemistry just from the phosphine.

original_title: Copper‐Catalyzed Enantioconvergent 1,4‐Difunctionalization of Homoallylic and Homopropargylic Alcohols via Radical‐Relay Deoxygenation
title: Turning a far-off hydroxyl into a handle for radical 1,4-difunctionalization
blurb: Homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols get deoxygenated and difunctionalized in one copper-catalyzed step, using a remote hydrogen-atom-transfer relay to link the OH and the alkene or alkyne sitting several carbons away, and it's enantioconvergent to boot. The relay step linking two non-adjacent groups is the actual trick here.

original_title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis
title: Peptide synthesis that runs N-to-C instead of the usual C-to-N
blurb: A continuous route for building peptides in the direction opposite to standard solid-phase synthesis. The flipped direction is the whole headline; there's not much else to go on beyond that framing.

original_title: Transition-Metal-Free Amination of Aryl Halides via Facile Aryne Generation
title: Skipping the metal catalyst for aryl halide amination, arynes do the work instead
blurb: KHMDS plus an 18-crown-6 additive generates arynes directly from aryl halides, which then get aminated with no transition metal involved, dodging the steric sensitivity and heterocycle poisoning that dog the usual metal-catalyzed routes. Worth it if the scope holds past the substrates shown.

original_title: Photoredox Decarboxylative Halogen Atom Transfer Strategy for C(sp2)–O/N Bond Construction
title: Indole-3-carboxylates and amides via a decarboxylation/halogen-relay cascade
blurb: A metal-free, visible-light photocatalytic route builds indole-3-carboxylates and amides from indolyl-alpha-keto acids by running decarboxylation into halogen-atom transfer into nucleophilic substitution with alcohols or amines. No stoichiometric activators, no metal catalyst, which is the whole pitch for these drug-relevant scaffolds.

original_title: Expanding 4′‐Thiomodification in Cyclic Dinucleotides for Potent STING Activation
title: Swapping another oxygen for sulfur to make STING agonists stickier
blurb: Having already shown that replacing the 4'-oxygen with sulfur stabilizes c-di-AMP and boosts its STING activity, the authors push the same swap into other cyclic dinucleotides. Incremental, but it matters if you're trying to keep these second messengers intact long enough to work as cancer immunotherapy or vaccine adjuvants.

original_title: Enantioselective Radical Difunctionalization of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes via Carbonyl Catalysis: Access to Multisubstituted Cyclobutanes
title: Getting bicyclobutanes to pop open asymmetrically
blurb: Carbonyl catalysis brings enantioselectivity to radical addition across bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes, yielding multisubstituted cyclobutanes with actual stereocontrol instead of none. Cyclobutanes are handy as rigid bioisosteres for aromatic rings, and the asymmetric version of this reaction has been the missing piece.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: An Intermediary Arene Dearomatization Approach for meta -Selective Functionalization of Arenols and Heteroarenols with O - and N -Nucleophiles
title: Dodging the ortho/para bias to hit meta on arenols for once
blurb: Electrophilic aromatic substitution always wants ortho or para on arenols and heteroarenols because of the alcohol's own electronics. This two-step, one-pot dihalogenative dearomatization routes around that to install O- and N-nucleophiles meta to the alcohol instead, under mild conditions, giving a substitution pattern EAS can't reach directly.

original_title: Photothermal Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution via a Traceless Carboxylate Directing Group
title: A carboxylate that activates the ring, then disappears
blurb: SNAr on arenes without the usual electron-withdrawing groups is normally a nonstarter, so this installs an ortho-carboxylate as a traceless handle, hits it with red light and cheap carbon black to aminate, then decarboxylates the handle off. Works on electronically neutral and electron-rich aryl bromides with primary amines, anilines and cyclic secondary amines, no transition metal needed.

original_title: Enantioselective Coupling of 1,3‐Dienes and Vinyl Acetate for the Synthesis of Succinic Acids and β‐ and γ‐Amino Acids
title: Dienes plus vinyl acetate, with cobalt doing the stereochemistry
blurb: A cationic Co(I) catalyst heterodimerizes 1,3-dienes with vinyl carboxylates, two cheap electron-rich feedstocks, into skipped 1,4-dienes with a single new stereocenter flanked by two differentiated double bonds, er typically above 96:4. The ligand, a P-centered chiral MeO-BIBOP, is commercially available, which is more than you can say for most asymmetric ligands worth bothering with. Sets up succinic acid and β/γ-amino acid synthesis from there.

original_title: Synthesis of ethylenediamines via reductive coupling of benzaldehydes and anilines by heterogeneous MHAT catalysis
title: Ethylenediamines from benzaldehydes and anilines, no homogeneous catalyst needed
blurb: Reductive coupling of benzaldehydes with anilines via heterogeneous MHAT catalysis builds ethylenediamines, swapping the usual homogeneous setup for something you can presumably filter off and reuse.

original_title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
title: Hexa-substituted benzenes, built through non-classical carbocations
blurb: A route to fully substituted benzene rings that runs through non-classical carbocation intermediates instead of the usual stabilized kind. Getting six substituents on one ring in a single method is usually earned the hard way, substrate by substrate.

original_title: Ru(II)-Catalyzed Regioselective [3+2] Annulation: Access to Spiro-Benzazepinoindolo Indenes
title: A ruthenium [3+2] that bolts an indene spiro ring onto steroid scaffolds
blurb: [Ru(p-cymene)Cl2]2 catalyzes a regioselective [3+2] spiroannulation of benzazepinoindoles with ynones, ynoates and ynamides, building hexacyclic spiro-indene fused products, including conjugates hung off cholesterol and l-menthol. Broad scope, X-ray structures to back it up, and they isolated the ruthenacyclic intermediate so the mechanism isn't just hand-waving.

original_title: Dual-functional interfacial architecture for PEG-based antifouling and protein G-mediated antibody orientation in sensitive immunoassays.
title: An antifouling surface that also points the antibody the right way
blurb: An interfacial coating doing two jobs at once: a PEG layer to keep nonspecific junk off the surface, and protein G to orient the captured antibodies, aimed at squeezing more sensitivity out of immunoassays.

original_title: Synthesis of α-Arylthioacetyloximes via TBN-Promoted Radical Difunctionalization of Aryl Alkenes with Disulfides
title: A metal-free radical route to sulfur oximes, with the mechanism nailed down
blurb: TBN drives a radical difunctionalization of aryl alkenes with disulfides, no transition metal, just mild heat, giving α-arylthioacetyloximes in moderate to good yields. TEMPO trapping and radical clock experiments confirm the radical pathway, and it holds up at 2 mmol scale, not just a milligram curiosity.

original_title: Cobalt-Catalyzed Oxygen-Ligand Transfer to Carbon Radicals
title: Getting oxygen onto a carbon radical without hydroxyl rebound
blurb: Most radical C-O bond formation runs through hydroxyl rebound, which only ever gets you hydroxyl transfer. This cobalt/photoredox system instead pairs cobalt-hydride HAT with a radical acyloxy migration to build a tertiary radical, then hands it an oxygen ligand straight off a cobalt(III)-oxygen complex. Opens up remote, Markovnikov-selective oxygenation the rebound mechanism just can't reach.

original_title: Chemical Synthesis in Flow Systems: Modern Approaches in the Pharmaceutical Industry
title: A review lap around pharma's flow chemistry push
blurb: A broad overview of continuous-flow synthesis for APIs and intermediates, covering the usual case for ditching batch processing: tighter control over reaction conditions, better safety, more throughput. No new data here, just a survey of where the field has landed.

original_title: A Retrospective study of ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT for predicting immunochemotherapy response and differentiating tumor residue in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
title: Can an FDG PET scan tell you a nasopharyngeal tumor is actually gone
blurb: A retrospective study using 18F-FDG PET/CT to predict response to immunochemotherapy and to distinguish leftover tumor from scar tissue in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Chart review rather than a trial, but that's usually how these imaging questions get a first answer.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Cu(OTf)2-Catalyzed Tandem Annulation of Arylamine-Substituted Maleimides and Aldehydes to Bispyrrole-Fused 1,4-Dihydropyridines
title: Two maleimides, one aldehyde, and a bispyrrole fused ring falls out
blurb: Cu(OTf)2 and p-TsOH push arylamine maleimides and aromatic aldehydes through condensation and cyclization, kicking out one arylamine along the way, to land selectively on bispyrrole-fused 1,4-dihydropyridines. One pot, decent selectivity claimed, though it's one substrate class so far.

original_title: Intrinsic Catalyst Reactivity—not Matched Surfactant Polarity—Drives Yield Differences in Aqueous Cross‐Coupling
title: The micelles were never doing the work you thought
blurb: Everyone assumes micelles in aqueous Suzuki couplings earn their keep by colocalizing reactants, matched to surfactant polarity. FLIM imaging on a fluorescent-product coupling says no, the catalyst's own reactivity explains the yield differences, not how well the surfactant matches it. Worth remembering before tuning the wrong knob at scale.

original_title: Spin and Charge Engineering of a BiCuMn Nanoalloy Catalyst for Industrial‐Scale Electrosynthesis of Glycine
title: A Bi-Cu-Mn alloy that electrosynthesizes glycine at industrial current
blurb: Atomically dispersed Cu and Mn on a Bi nanoalloy for electrocatalytic C-N coupling to glycine. Cu tweaks the Bi sites via d-p hybridization to grab nitrogen species, Mn kicks in spin-polarized electrons for the nitrogen oxide intermediate, and together they're claimed to fix the selectivity and durability problems that usually show up once you push to real current densities.

original_title: Ligand-specific binding kinetics and molecular interactions of clinically used PSMA diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals: an integrated in silico and in vitro study.
title: How PSMA tracers actually grip their target, modeled and measured
blurb: An in silico plus in vitro look at the binding kinetics and molecular interactions behind the PSMA radiopharmaceuticals already used in the clinic for diagnosis.

original_title: Supramolecular Hexaphyrin Cage: Cooperative Guest Binding and Reversible Aromaticity Switching by Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
title: A hexaphyrin cage that flips its own aromaticity on demand
blurb: Pt(II) corners pin two antiaromatic hexaphyrin decks into a trigonal-prismatic cage, confirmed as a single symmetric assembly by NMR, mass spec, and DOSY. The cage binds guests cooperatively and switches aromaticity reversibly through proton-coupled electron transfer, so it's a cage that changes its electronic character rather than just its shape.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Anion‐Site Coupling Programs Interfacial Hydration for Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation
title: Turns out the anions at the electrode aren't just spectating
blurb: The usual assumption is that anions get shoved away from a charged cathode and don't matter. Here Cu2+ sites on carbon black grab onto bicarbonate specifically over carbonate or sulfate, reshaping the water layer at the interface and speeding up electrocatalytic hydrogenation near neutral pH. A passive-ion assumption quietly wrong.

original_title: Construction of benzochalcogenaboroles via single-atom editing of boracycles
title: Editing one atom in a boracycle opens up a new boron ring family
blurb: Flipping a benzoboretene back and forth with a boron-carbon diradical, a 'diradical reservoir,' gives modular access to three classes of benzochalcogenaborole skeletons. Some of them show up as ferroptosis inhibitors, which is the actual hook here: skeletal editing on boron rings reaching straight into biological activity.

original_title: Elizabeth Smyth, MD, on Gastric/GEJ Cancer: Novel CLDN18.2-Targeting ADC - The ASCO Post
title: An oncologist's take on the new CLDN18.2 ADC in gastric cancer
blurb: Elizabeth Smyth walks through the novel CLDN18.2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate in gastric and GEJ cancer, expert commentary rather than a new dataset.

original_title: Radical Ring-Opening Polymerization of endo -Cyclic Monomers for Regioregularity Control in Vinyl Polymers
title: Breaking vinyl polymers out of their head-to-tail habit
blurb: Radical polymerization almost always locks vinyl backbones into head-to-tail connectivity. This group runs radical ring-opening polymerization on endo-cyclic monomers, a class nobody's really used for rROP, and gets carbon-carbon backbones with regioregularity you can't reach the normal way, not the usual cleavable-linkage trick other rROP systems chase.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Biomimetic N ‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
title: A photoredox route to the amino acid homologs everyone skipped
blurb: Beta3-amino acids have good decarboxylative routes, beta2 homologs have been the neglected sibling. This uses photoredox catalysis and a radical translocation cascade to homologate amino acids at the N-terminus, biomimetically, reaching the beta2 class that lead optimization chemists have been missing a general method for.

original_title: Continuous Flow Synthesis of α‐Diazocarbonyl Reagents by Diazo Transfer Reaction Using a Supported Base
title: A safer assembly line for diazo compounds
blurb: Diazo transfer run in continuous flow over a reusable polystyrene-supported base that doubles as a scavenger, turning out a clean diazo stream (including the nitro-ester version) with no byproducts to strip out. That stream feeds straight into a rhodium-catalyzed cyclopropanation. The whole point of flow here is keeping unstable diazo intermediates out of a flask in bulk, which is the usual reason anyone bothers.

original_title: Fe-Photocatalyzed Alkenylation and Alkynylation of α-Heteroatom Radicals from Carboxylic Acids and Unsaturated Sulfones
title: Iron picks up the photocatalyst job from iridium
blurb: Visible light plus a cheap iron salt drives decarboxylative alkenylation and alkynylation of amino acids and other alpha-heteroatom carboxylic acids, using alkenyl and alkynyl sulfones as the radical traps. No ligand, no added oxidant, and the scope reads wide. Mostly notable for what it doesn't need: the usual precious-metal photocatalyst.

original_title: Naphthalimide–Naphthalene Diimide Dyads with a Hydrazinyl Linker: Amphoteric Multi-state Redox, Radical Ions, Self-assembly, and Intramolecular Carbonyl–Carbonyl Non-covalent Contacts
title: Getting naphthalimide and naphthalene diimide to actually talk to each other
blurb: Swap the usual floppy linker for a rigid hydrazinyl one and the NDI and NMI halves start sharing electrons instead of just sitting next to each other. An accessible oxidation on that linker opens up amphoteric multi-redox behavior, stable radical ions, and intramolecular carbonyl-carbonyl contacts that also drive self-assembly. A structure paper more than anything, but it shows the linker choice actually matters electronically.

original_title: Electrons Follow Mysterious Pathways: Cyclic Delocalization versus Electron Sharing
title: Why nobody agrees which ring in coronene is aromatic
blurb: Delocalization indices are supposed to tell you which circuit in a polycyclic molecule carries the aromaticity, but different indices pick different rings for the same molecule. Working through coronene and free-base porphyrin, the authors show the ring-ordered multicenter index is just the geometric mean of the pi bond orders around the loop, so a few strongly shared bonds can paper over several weak ones. That's a tidy explanation for the disagreement: the indices aren't measuring the same kind of average.

original_title: Turnovers Drive Supported Metal Nanoparticle Catalyst Surface Reconstruction to Kinetically Trapped Metastable Structures
title: Catalysts don't settle down, they get stuck
blurb: The standard assumption is that a supported nanoparticle catalyst's surface structure and adsorbate coverage settle into whatever thermodynamics favors. This argues that under high coverage and fast turnover, the surface instead gets kinetically trapped in a metastable arrangement that never reaches that equilibrium state. If right, the clean, pre-characterized catalyst structure people study beforehand may just not be the one doing the actual chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: MS1-Based Chromatographic Alignment Improves Retention Time Prediction for Multiplexed Targeted Proteomics
title: Targeted proteomics stops needing a calibration run
blurb: GoDig's retention time predictions currently lean on an elution-order calibration step. Swapping in MS1 alignment-based priming instead identifies and quantifies more targets, skips the calibration MS2 scans and real-time search entirely, and holds up better against chromatographic drift. Fewer scans spent on bookkeeping, more on the targets you actually care about.

original_title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
title: Glycosyl radicals that don't need a redox additive to show up
blurb: Bench-stable glycosyl sulfonohydrazides, made catalytically without stoichiometric reagents, hand off to a nickel catalyst that breaks the anomeric C-N bond and generates the glycosyl radical on its own, no external oxidant or reductant required. That radical then couples stereoselectively, which is the part radical glycosylation has usually struggled with.

original_title: In Situ Formation of CF3–Hemiketal HDDA Substrates Enables Ambient-Temperature, Three-Component, Benzyne Cascade Reactions
title: Benzynes made at room temperature, no catalyst in sight
blurb: Mix propargylic diynes with trifluoromethyl ketone diynes and the CF3 group's electron pull is enough on its own to spontaneously stitch them into tetraynes, which then cyclize to benzynes at room temperature with no catalyst needed. A trapping agent closes out the cascade in one pot. Also neat: the TIPS group installed just to control regiochemistry turns out to pull double duty in the cascade.

original_title: Overcoming substrate constraints to unlock chiral dihydropyridines for stereodefined piperidine synthesis
title: Chiral dihydropyridines without the electron-withdrawing crutch
blurb: Asymmetric dearomatization of pyridines has always needed an electron-withdrawing substituent to work, which boxes in what you can make. A rhodium-catalyzed addition of boronic acids to N-alkylpyridinium salts drops that requirement, so plain pyridines react with aryl, heteroaryl, and alkenyl boronic acids in high yield and enantioselectivity. Opens stereodefined piperidine synthesis to substrates that were off limits before.

original_title: Trimethoprim metabolites and formation of protein adducts.
title: Trimethoprim's metabolites and the protein adducts they leave behind
blurb: A review of what trimethoprim breaks down into in the body and how those metabolites go on to form adducts with proteins.

original_title: Supramolecular Assemblies of Dendritic Polycarboxylates With Distinct Morphologies for Antiviral Inhibition
title: Shape, not just surface chemistry, decides how well these dendrimers block viruses
blurb: Hyperbranched and perfectly dendritic polyglycerol cores, both capped with the same thiol acid, self-assemble into distinct morphologies and get tested as broad-spectrum antivirals. The interesting bit is that the backbone architecture itself seems to tune inhibition, not just the usual surface tweaking.

original_title: Combination Strategies with Lutetium-177 PSMA in Advanced Prostate Cancer - Shahneen Sandhu - UroToday
title: Where the Lu-177 PSMA combination trials actually stand
blurb: Sandhu runs through the various combination strategies being tried alongside Lu-177 PSMA in advanced prostate cancer. A talk rounding up the field rather than a new dataset, so don't expect fresh numbers here.

original_title: Mechanism of Alkene Skeletal Isomerization in Zeolites Revealed by Coupled‐Cluster Accurate Free‐Energy Simulations
title: Settling the carbocation argument in zeolite catalysis with CCSD(T)-grade dynamics
blurb: Whether Brønsted acid-catalyzed alkene isomerization in zeolites actually runs through stable carbocation intermediates has been argued over for years, mostly because nobody could afford coupled-cluster-accurate free energies on a dynamics timescale. This gets there by pairing a QM/QM learning scheme with a machine-learned potential to run near-CCSD(T) simulations. A computational answer to a mechanistic fight that's been stuck on cost, not ideas.

original_title: Complete biosynthesis and production of paclitaxel in a plant host
title: Taxol's full biosynthesis pathway, finally run start to finish in a plant
blurb: Paclitaxel's biosynthesis has stayed partly unmapped for decades despite the drug's cost. This reconstructs and chemically validates the complete pathway in a model plant, works out the compartment-to-compartment trafficking steps that were the missing piece, and pushes production up in tobacco. If those yields carry over past this one host, that's a real dent in why the drug is expensive in the first place.

original_title: Size-tunable and surface-functionalized hydrophilic magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles prepared by one-pot synthesis.
title: Magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles with the size dial built in
blurb: A one-pot synthesis for hydrophilic iron oxide nanoparticles that lets you tune particle size and surface functionalization at the same time, rather than bolting the surface chemistry on afterward. That's the whole pitch, no application data to go with it.

original_title: Hydrogel-Based Biomaterials for Oral Ulcer Repair: Structural Design, Critical Properties, Therapeutic Mechanisms, and Translational Challenges.
title: A hydrogel roadmap for patching up mouth ulcers
blurb: A review walking through hydrogel biomaterials for oral ulcer repair: structural design choices, which properties actually matter, the mechanisms behind the healing effect, and the usual gap between bench results and clinical translation. A survey, not a new material.

original_title: Biointerface-Engineered Screen-Printed Electrodes Enable Wild-Type P450 BM3 Bioelectrochemistry for Myristic Acid Sensing
title: Getting a wild-type P450 to actually talk to a screen-printed electrode
blurb: Printed electrodes usually kill electron transfer from immobilized enzymes because the binder gets in the way. Here Ar plasma treatment strips down that binder interference and a DDAB layer gives wild-type P450 BM3 a compatible home, on disposable graphite electrodes tuned for sensing myristic acid. A biointerface fix aimed squarely at the thing that's been limiting these sensors.

original_title: Sialic Acid-Functionalized CuS for Efficient Prevention and Treatment of H3N2 Viral Infections
title: Sialic acid-dressed copper sulfide nanoparticles going after H3N2
blurb: Copper sulfide nanoparticles get lactose acid linked on via SH-PEG-NH2, then sialic acid enzymatically conjugated onto the galactose, so the particles mimic the receptor flu actually binds and block H3N2 before and after infection. The decoy logic tracks, but it's still a nanoparticle paper, so mind the gap to an actual patient.

original_title: Mechanistic Insights into Ni(I)–Isocyanide Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Reactions: A Density Functional Theory Study of Reactivity and Selectivity
title: Why Ni(I)-isocyanide catalysts pick Kumada over the alternative
blurb: A DFT study working out why Ni(I)-isocyanide catalyzed cross-couplings favor the Kumada pathway over competing routes. Pure mechanism, nickel being the cheap, earth-abundant stand-in everyone's been poking at instead of palladium, no new reaction here, just the reasoning for why it goes that way.

original_title: Synthesis of Chiral Pyrrolo[3,2,1- ij ]quinolines by Rh-Catalyzed Asymmetric Arylation/Acid-Promoted Condensation Sequence
title: Chiral pyrrolo quinolines, now without organocatalysis
blurb: This scaffold had only ever been made asymmetrically via organocatalysis. Here a rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric arylation of β-indol-7-yl enones with arylboronic acids, followed by an acid-promoted condensation in the same pot, gets chiral pyrrolo[3,2,1-ij]quinolines in high yield and high ee instead, the first transition-metal route to the molecule.

original_title: Skeletal Editing of Pyrimidines to Access 3-(Alkylthio)pyridines
title: Turning pyrimidines into pyridines, one ring-opening at a time
blurb: A skeletal editing route that swaps a pyrimidine's ring for a pyridine, installing a C3 thioether along the way with sulfonium salts as the key synthon. The ring opens to an aza-streptocyanine intermediate, picks up an in-situ sulfur ylide, and closes back down, leaving the C2 and C6 substituents independently variable. Scaffold hopping with an actual mechanistic story behind it rather than just a reaction that happens to work.

original_title: Proton Relays Versus Direct Transfer in Polyketide Cyclisations: Solution Rejection, Bioinspired Complexes, and Enzyme-Pocket Rescue
title: Why polyketide cyclizations skip the proton relay
blurb: A comparison of whether polyketide-cyclizing enzymes move protons directly or hand them off through a relay, tested with bioinspired model complexes and enzyme-pocket mimics standing in for the real active site. The relay gets rejected in solution, it apparently takes the enzyme pocket to rescue it.

original_title: A prospective comparison of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT for evaluating viable brain metastases in lung cancer.
title: FAPI PET might see brain mets that FDG washes out
blurb: A prospective head-to-head testing Ga-FAPI-2286 against FDG PET/CT for spotting viable brain metastases in lung cancer. FDG has always had the problem that the brain lights up on its own and buries small mets in that background, so a tracer without that noise is worth the comparison. Still one prospective study, not a reason to swap tracers yet.

original_title: Aqueous π‐Hole Interactions Enabled by Chiral Perfluoroarene Amphiphiles
title: Chiral perfluoroarene amphiphiles that still do pi-hole chemistry in water
blurb: Octafluoronaphthalene-based amphiphiles built so arene-perfluoroarene pi-hole interactions, usually a dry, solvent-free trick, hold up and self-assemble in water instead. End-group tweaks tune the amphiphilicity and the confined microenvironment inside the assemblies. Getting AP interactions to behave in water is the actual point, not just another molecular recognition paper.

original_title: Catalytic Asymmetric Carbamoylation: Carbamoyl Sources, Activation Modes, and Stereocontrol.
title: A review of how chemists get carbamoylation to go asymmetric
blurb: A survey of catalytic asymmetric carbamoylation covering the carbamoyl sources in use, how they get activated, and what's actually setting the stereochemistry. Handy as a field summary, but it's a review, not a new result.

original_title: Direct Organozirconium‐Catalyzed Copolymerization of Propylene with Phosphino‐Olefins: Access to Isotactic Phosphine‐Functionalized Polypropylenes for Diverse Functions
title: Polypropylene that comes pre-loaded with phosphine handles
blurb: An ansa-bis(indenyl)zirconium catalyst copolymerizes propylene directly with phosphino-olefins, giving isotactic polypropylene with phosphine groups built in at up to 2.0 mol% incorporation. It still hits turnover frequencies up to 2940 kg/(mol·h·atm) at 25°C, which is fast for a functional comonomer that usually poisons catalysts like this one. Functionalized polypropylene has been a hard target for exactly that reason, so a route that keeps both the catalyst alive and the tacticity intact is the news.

original_title: Substrate Promiscuity of an Acetyltransferase Drives Euphorbia Diterpenoid Diversity in Petty Spurge
title: One enzyme, one plant, and most of its diterpenoid diversity
blurb: In petty spurge, a single BAHD acetyltransferase, Ep17169, turns out to acetylate both macrocyclic jatrophane and polycyclic ingenane diterpenoid scaffolds. That kind of substrate promiscuity is apparently enough on its own to explain much of the plant's acylated diterpenoid diversity. Those acetyl groups aren't decoration either, they're what set the multidrug-resistance-reversal and anticancer activity, so one sloppy enzyme covering multiple scaffolds is a tidier story than a dedicated enzyme for each.
